subject: Post-call recap: buying channel & procurement next steps (AWS Marketplace vs PO)
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Melanie Torres <melanie.torres@aurorahealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-15 09:12 PST
Subject: Post-call recap: buying channel & procurement next steps (AWS Marketplace vs PO)

Hi Melanie — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so procurement and cloud ops have a clean handoff: 

- Aurora showed clear preference for an AWS Marketplace purchase (consolidated billing + internal approvals flow).
- Procurement asked whether we can (A) support Marketplace SaaS listing for a subscription purchase or (B) accept a customer PO & direct invoicing if Marketplace approval will take longer.
- Legal/InfoSec flagged the need for an MSA review (they prefer our standard MSA or an AWS Marketplace agreement).
- Estimated timeline from your side: procurement approval ~30–45 days if Marketplace goes smoothly; direct PO route could be 2–4 weeks if finance is ready.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll send a short Marketplace onboarding checklist + pricing estimate for procurement to review (attached).
2) If procurement wants Marketplace, I’ll loop in our Marketplace onboarding lead and share the AWS listing guide.
3) If PO is required, we can send a DocuSign-ready MSA + invoice flow and confirm billing contact.
4) Schedule a 30-min sync next week with your procurement + cloud ops to align on the channel decision and timeline.

Please confirm: preferred buying channel (Marketplace vs PO) and the procurement contact who will own the review. I’ll follow up with attachments and a proposed meeting slot.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this moving.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

Vanessa — thanks for the crisp recap. A few clarifications from my side: 

- Aurora Procurement strongly prefers AWS Marketplace for SaaS where possible because it reduces internal PO churn and ties to our consolidated AWS bill.
- That said, Finance will accept a PO if Marketplace listing cannot be completed quickly; the key requirement is that the vendor accepts our PO terms (net 30) or signs our standard addendum.
- Our cloud ops team wants to confirm that a Marketplace subscription will allow us to use PrivateLink and that data residency/telemetry aligns with our controls. I’ll loop them into the next call.

Procurement owner: Jordan Herrera (procurement@aurorahealth.com). He’ll take the lead on timeline and vendor onboarding.

Let’s tentatively plan for the Marketplace path — please send the onboarding checklist and the Marketplace guide so Jordan can kick off the approval. If Marketplace looks like it will take >30 days, we’ll fall back to PO.

—Melanie

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Melanie Torres <melanie.torres@aurorahealth.com>
Cc: Jordan Herrera <procurement@aurorahealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-16 08:45 PST
Subject: Marketplace checklist + pricing estimate (attachments)

Melanie / Jordan — attaching three files to help procurement and cloud ops: marketplace_onboarding_checklist.pdf, redwood_pricing_estimate_v2.xlsx, aws_mp_listing_guide.pdf. Summary of the important bits below.

Key differences between paths:
- AWS Marketplace (preferred):
  * Pros: consolidated billing, faster internal approvals for your teams, simplified vendor onboarding once listing is live.
  * What we need from you: AWS account ID for listing (or permission to create a private listing), procurement point-of-contact for the Marketplace registration form, and confirmation that using Marketplace SaaS meets your telemetry/residency requirements.
  * Typical timeline: 2–4 weeks for basic listing + procurement review; 4–6 weeks if legal requires custom addenda.

- Direct PO / invoicing (fallback):
  * Pros: can be faster if your finance is ready to issue a PO and accept our standard terms.
  * What we need: completed purchase order, billing contact, and a signed MSA (DocuSign link below).
  * Typical timeline: 1–3 weeks for PO processing once MSA is agreed.

Attached pricing spreadsheet includes both subscription SKU (Marketplace-style monthly) and a direct invoiced option with payment terms and seat tiers. We listed rough numbers for 6/12/24-month commitments to help procurement model costs.

Action items I’ll take this week:
- Loop in our Marketplace onboarding specialist (Laura) to start the AWS listing intake.
- Send DocuSign MSA if you want to prepare a PO fallback.
- Propose two calendar slots for a 30-min joint sync (I’ll share in a follow-up).

DocuSign link for MSA (if going PO route): https://docusign.net/link/RW-MSA-2026-AUR-347
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/347

Thanks — I’ll wait for Jordan to confirm the buying path and share his availability.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-11-16 10:10 PST
Subject: Re: Marketplace checklist + pricing estimate (attachments)

Melanie/Jordan — quick technical note from our side on the PrivateLink question:

- Redwood supports customer-specific networking options. For a Marketplace subscription, we can enable PrivateLink-backed connections for model serving (there is a one-time setup and a small infra fee).
- Data residency/telemetry: we can restrict logs/telemetry to your VPC and export audit logs to your CloudWatch account; we’ll document exact data flows for your InfoSec review.

If you confirm Marketplace, we’ll prepare a short runbook and an architecture appendix that procurement/infosec can attach. Happy to present that to your cloud ops team on the next call.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions | Redwood Inference

1) Jordan will send the AWS account ID privately to Vanessa this afternoon (we do private listing first).
2) Legal wants to see the Marketplace terms + our standard addendum; if Marketplace listing requires different language, Jordan will escalate to our legal.
3) Timeline: procurement expects to complete internal approvals in ~3 weeks assuming no legal exceptions; if legal asks for changes, we’ll get back with expected delays.

Jordan — please confirm once you’ve started the AWS intake. Vanessa — once you have Jordan’s AWS account ID I think Laura should start the AWS intake form and we can schedule a 30-min alignment with procurement + cloud ops next Tue or Wed.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Melanie
